# MindAttic.Orchestrator — User Stories
> ✅ done (shipped & tested) · 🟡 partial · ⬜ planned. Every ✅ cites the test.

## Priority backlog
_Nothing recorded yet._


## Epic A — MindAttic.Orchestrator.Desktop.Maui: a Blazor Hybrid UI shell alongside WPF
- **M.ORCH-US-A1 ⬜** As a maintainer, every UI component is defined once by a shared component spec (visual design/style + its editable property API) that drives all three implementations — WPF, Blazor (MAUI shell), and MindAttic.Components.Web (HTML/CSS/JS) — so the three always render with identical look and feel and expose identical editable properties; editing the spec regenerates or re-verifies all three so they never drift out of sync.
- **M.ORCH-US-A2 ⬜** As a maintainer, I can define a UI component once in a shared spec (its name, visual design/styling tokens, states, and editable property/event API) that drives two generated outputs: (1) shared HTML/CSS/JS markup consumed directly by both the MindAttic.Components.Web component and the Blazor component (Blazor adds only a thin .razor/C# wrapper for data binding and events, reusing the same markup and styles rather than a separate copy), and (2) a generated WPF control (XAML + code-behind) with matching look, states, and the same editable property/event API; editing the spec is what keeps all three in sync, instead of maintaining three hand-written implementations.


## Epic B — Lock/unlock a login
- **M.ORCH-US-B1 ✅** As the owner, I can Lock any real login (a per-CLI one or the global login, never the API key) by right-clicking it, so the orchestrator can't open a CLI on it, dispatch or move work to it, or keep its CLIs running, until I Unlock it; a login also locks itself the moment it reaches its own weekly cutoff, even past an active org allow, and stays locked past its weekly reset until I unlock it (never automatically). A locked login stays shown in the tree and tab strip with a red lock badge, and orchestrator org lock/unlock/locks do the same from the CLI. *(verified by `Locking_adds_the_login_and_logs_it`, `AutoLock_fires_at_the_cutoff_whatever_an_active_org_allow_says`, `AutoLock_leaves_the_login_locked_after_the_weekly_reset_passes`, `A_locked_login_is_paced_to_a_stop_until_unlocked`, `A_locked_login_is_never_a_move_target`, `Org_start_refuses_a_locked_login_the_same_way_start_account_does`, `The_activity_word_says_who_locked_a_login_and_why`, `A_login_that_crosses_its_weekly_cutoff_is_locked_skipped_and_stopped_until_an_explicit_unlock`.)*

Stored in %APPDATA%\MindAttic\MindAttic.Orchestrator\accounts.json, separate from the per-account token ledger. | M.ORCH-T561 | 2026-10-20 | feature | closed | A subagent is released as soon as its LLM work is done: it builds, runs only the tests its change touches, commits, lands on main and closes its ticket, then /allocate hands its slot the next ticket; it no longer waits on the full suite (often 20+ minutes that spend no tokens). The orchestrator daemon runs each repo's full test suite on main itself, with no LLM, after each landing (several landings coalesced into one run, none running while one is already going for that repo), and files one --type fix ticket per failing test (test name, failure message, the commits landed since the last green run) only when tests fail; a test already open as a ticket isn't filed twice, and one that passes again closes its ticket. The claim prompt orchestrator next prints says this instead of telling the subagent to wait for the full run | e450bed |
| M.ORCH-T562 | 2026-10-20 | feature | closed | A failing-test fix ticket from the background full-suite run (M.ORCH-T561) goes to the top of the queue: it is filed with a priority above every other open ticket in the workspace, so the next free subagent slot in any CLI running /allocate takes it before anything else; with several failing, they keep the order they failed in, all ahead of every other ticket. The ticket names the landed tickets whose commits were in the run, so the fix starts from what just changed | 71fa931 |
| M.ORCH-T563 | 2026-10-20 | feature | closed | orchestrator next --claim picks a model for each ticket it hands out and prints it with the prompt, so /allocate starts that subagent on it: Sonnet 5.5 for fixes, failed-test tickets and tightly specified changes with a clear definition of done; Opus 5.5 for features, design work, changes across many files, and anything that must be right the first time. A per-repo or per-ticket override in settings wins. A Sonnet ticket whose diff is over a size limit, or touches files listed as risky (the gates, pacing, git landing), gets one Opus review of the diff only (no re-reading the repo) before it lands. The ticket's cost is recorded by model, so orchestrator report can compare cost per completed ticket between the two | ModelChoiceTests (cd7d25b) |

| M.ORCH-T635 | 2026-10-22 | fix | closed | Budget chart's "at reset" projection label is misleadingly rounded: UtilizationChartData.cs's ChartFor formats the projection as $"{u.ProjectedEndPercent:0}% at reset" (zero decimals), while the live reading right next to it uses one decimal ("now {Formatting.FiveHourPercent(u.NowPercent)}" e.g. "now 98.1%"). Reported case: current usage already 98.1% (over the 98% PaceTargetPercent default), yet the projection still displayed as a bare "98% at reset" because the underlying ProjectedEndPercent (something like 98.1-98.49) rounds down to 98, making an over-target landing look identical to hitting the target exactly. Pacing is supposed to land usage under PaceTargetPercent (98%) by reset, not somewhere between 98.0% and 99.0%, so the rounding is actively hiding a real overshoot from the user. Fix: give the projection label the same one-decimal precision as the "now" label (and double check Pacer's spentOut/atTarget stop-gate math isn't itself letting usage run past the target before reset, not just a display issue). | 462ab71 |

| M.ORCH-T747 | 2026-10-23 | fix | closed | No member's login is ever a fallback: under Claude Team billing, every CLI not started on a login of its own runs on the global ~/.claude login, which is a member's seat (Erin's now), and the dashboard marks it 'Erin (fallback)' (LoginScope.cs:111, StatusAggregator.cs:250, Redelegation.FallbackKey M.ORCH-T662/T672), so one person carries everyone's unassigned load. The owner: 'the API is the only fallback, no user should be burdened with another account's load'. Make the Vault API key the only fallback for CLIs without their own login (and redelegation), honouring M.ORCH-T706 (API billing only when the owner has it on; otherwise such work waits rather than landing on a member), treat the global login purely as its member's own seat, and drop '(fallback)' from any member's name | 266db30 |
| M.ORCH-T748 | 2026-10-23 | feature | closed | A background subagent dies silently whenever its host Claude Code process exits for any reason other than a budget-window reset (window closed, crash, sleep). The next session only sees a task-notification with status 'stopped' and 'no completion record found' — no alert at the time, no automatic recovery. The Orchestrator already resumes a CLI after its budget window resets (resume-after-reset); it has no equivalent for a host process disappearing mid-task. Add: (1) the daemon detects a dispatched ticket whose session/subagent went dark (process gone, no completion notification, ticket still open with no new Ref) rather than waiting for the human to notice on next session start; (2) it auto-redispatches that ticket's work (a fresh subagent in the same worktree, carrying forward the original ticket text and any research notes left in the worktree/docs) the same way a human operator did it by hand for RB-T74, RB-T76 and RB-T71 on 2026-10-23; (3) surface this as a distinct state (e.g. 'orphaned') in 'orchestrator status'/'orchestrator queue', separate from a normal open ticket, so it's visible immediately rather than only at the next SessionStart. Goal: /allocate-driven work keeps going whether or not the owner is watching, matching the existing promise for budget-window stops. | ae1c8ac (OrphanWatchTests) |

| M.ORCH-T801 | 2026-10-24 | fix | closed | Audit: round only for display, never before computing or gating. M.ORCH-T794 found BlockPercent lost precision because a token count was (long)-truncated mid-calculation and divided back into a percent (60% silently became 59.976%), and that truncated value fed pacing/gating decisions, not just the display. Sweep the budget/pacing code for the same anti-pattern -- any (long)/(int) cast, Math.Round, Math.Floor or Math.Truncate applied to a percent or token value before it's compared against a target/cutoff or fed into further math -- and fix each one to carry full double precision through every calculation and gating decision, rounding only at the final formatting/display step (CLI output, dashboard text). User principle (2026-10-24): show rounded numbers but measure with perfect precision. | c532641d |

| M.ORCH-T976 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | TermViewer reconnects although its doc says it never does (ViewerWindow.cs:163 vs :24): on a protocol-1 host it takes the session back from the dashboard every 0.5s until its presence check folds it, ping-ponging the screen; the 'fold when replaced' path is dead code for that case (found by bughunt) | 45577f3b |
| M.ORCH-T977 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | A --stay --watch pop-out holding a session's slot mutex stops FallbackViewers from opening an interactive fallback window when the dashboard goes down, leaving only a read-only window on that CLI (TermViewer Program.cs:40-45, FallbackViewers.cs:148) (found by bughunt) | f14c6dd7 |
| M.ORCH-T978 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | In a watch-only TermViewer window, OnPreviewKeyDown returns early when watchOnly (ViewerWindow.cs:294), so Ctrl+C with a selection doesn't copy: the renderer clears the selection and the host drops the input (found by bughunt) | 436647fa |
| M.ORCH-T979 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | Keys or a paste typed while a tab is reconnecting are dropped silently (RelayConnection.Send finds link null) but still marked handled: queue them until reconnect or show that input was not sent (found by bughunt) | 07348628 |
| M.ORCH-T980 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | Gateway StreamMasker copies escape sequences byte for byte (StreamMasker.cs:86-92), so secrets inside OSC 0/2 titles, OSC 8 hyperlinks, OSC 52 clipboard base64, DCS or APC strings go to remote viewers unmasked in Output and Replay (TermBridge.cs:260-285); mask printable payloads inside OSC/DCS/APC strings too (found by bughunt) | dbc36fa3 |
| M.ORCH-T981 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | Gateway GET /sessions returns the raw live title (GatewayApp.cs:148, from TermSession.cs:214) unmasked and even while the session is paused, leaking secrets in titles to every watcher (the team wall polls it every 10s); mask titles there and freeze them during pause (found by bughunt) | a388cb27 |
| M.ORCH-T982 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | Gateway masking misses secrets split by a hard line wrap, by a chunk boundary after punctuation, or by the 40ms flush (StreamMasker.cs:93-97,131,139-145; TermBridge.cs:248): Ink CLIs wrap long tokens with real newlines and slow output flushes before a token is long enough to match; hold candidate runs across newlines and flushes until they cannot be a known shape (found by bughunt) | ec3663ae |
| M.ORCH-T983 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | Gateway streams outlive their token: the bearer token is checked once at attach (GatewayApp.cs:173) and the loop at :219-239 re-checks only grants, so a 15-minute token keeps a stream open indefinitely and rotating signing.key does not close open streams; re-check token expiry and signing key in the watch loop (found by bughunt) | 12ed6105 |
| M.ORCH-T984 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | Gateway revocation watch dies for good after one exception: the catch at GatewayApp.cs:238 is outside the while loop, so any throw from AccessTo (e.g. a null entry in acl.json, GatewayGrants.cs:94,118) stops revocation checks and input auditing for that stream (fails open) (found by bughunt) | 2dc6057d |
| M.ORCH-T985 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | Gateway lets remote viewers attach to protocol-1 TermHosts (no session.Protocol check at GatewayApp.cs:175-191; only the client-side WallSession.Streamable checks), so any same-org member can repeatedly kick the owner's own tab off a single-viewer host (found by bughunt) | 70583441 |
| M.ORCH-T986 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | Gateway: one transient read error on acl.json or broadcast.json sticks until the file's text changes, because the stamp is updated before the read (GatewayGrants.cs:78-82, GatewayBroadcast.cs:55-58) and the daemon only rewrites on change, locking everyone out or unsharing all sessions; keep the last good settings and retry (found by bughunt) | 382c05a9 |
| M.ORCH-T987 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | Gateway login throttle (GatewayApp.cs:308-310) scans and locks the whole failure dictionary on every failure once more than 1024 addresses are tracked and never evicts recent entries (pre-auth CPU and memory growth); concurrent requests also slip past the 5-try limit (found by bughunt) | df6d6b21 |
| M.ORCH-T988 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | Gateway refusals for bad or expired tokens (GatewayApp.cs:139,173) and wrong owner keys (:117) are never written to term_audit, although the audit contract covers every refusal (found by bughunt) | f9e7b79a |
| M.ORCH-T989 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | orchestrator gateway revoke --session compares the session id case-sensitively on SQLite (TermGrants.cs:71) while the gateway matches case-insensitively (GatewayGrants.cs:101), so a revoke typed in a different case reports no such grant while the grant stays in force (found by bughunt) | c7259581 |
| M.ORCH-T990 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | TermHost logs the viewer-supplied ViewerId unsanitized (TermSession.cs:317, kept by the gateway at TermBridge.cs:144), so any viewer, watchers included, can forge host log lines with embedded newlines (found by bughunt) | 844a503b |
| M.ORCH-T991 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | TermHost resizes a closed pseudoconsole: WatchExit calls ClosePseudoConsole(hPC) without zeroing hPC and waits up to 2s before setting exited (TermSession.cs:229-235), so a Resize or Nudge in that window calls ResizePseudoConsole on freed memory (:504-575), crashing the host (no Exit frame, registry entry left) or corrupting another handle (found by bughunt) | 61f940db |
| M.ORCH-T992 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | TermHost ApplySize and Nudge update cols/rows and the emulator under the lock but call SetPtySize after releasing it (TermSession.cs:505,512,555), so concurrent resizes (owner Resize vs TakeSize or owner hand-over) can reach the ConPTY in the wrong order, leaving the PTY at the old size while viewers, registry and emulator have the new one (found by bughunt) | e610ab16 |
| M.ORCH-T993 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | TermHost merges every interactive viewer's automatic replies as input (TermSession.cs:462-490, ViewerPolicy.cs:68-79): focus reports ESC[I/ESC[O and DSR/DA replies from several viewers reach the CLI (it ends up unfocused; each query gets N replies shown as garbage at the prompt) and fire ownership changes; accept focus and query replies from the size owner only (found by bughunt) | 18e906fb |
| M.ORCH-T994 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | TermHost sends the emulator snapshot as one Replay frame that can exceed ViewerLink's 32MB MaxBacklog (ViewerLink.cs:52 vs TermSession.cs:358-362), so a viewer of a session with heavily styled scrollback is disposed on every attach and can never attach; cap or chunk the snapshot (found by bughunt) | 04debfc2 |
| M.ORCH-T995 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | TermSessions.Enumerate deletes a live host's registry file when Read hits an IOException five times in 100ms (antivirus or indexer holding it), treating it as junk older than a minute (Term/TermSessions.cs:76-88,118-121), hiding the session from discovery; never delete on read failure, only when the host process is gone (found by bughunt) | 061ffa53 |
| M.ORCH-T996 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | TermHost's cmd.exe /d /c wrapping quotes argv only for CommandLineToArgvW (HostOptions.cs:126, Native.Quote) and does not escape cmd metacharacters, so an argv caller passing an argument with & \| ^ % runs extra commands (not reachable from the dashboard today, which passes one -EncodedCommand) (found by bughunt) | 9331f41c |
| M.ORCH-T997 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | TermHost broadcasts Exit 2s after the CLI exits even if the output pump has not reached EOF (TermSession.cs:230-238), so heavy final output can arrive after Exit and be lost when the host leaves 500ms later; wait for the pump to drain before Exit (found by bughunt) | 978aa85e |
| M.ORCH-T998 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | TermHost's raw ring trims at an arbitrary byte when full (Replay/Ring.cs:44-46), so a ring replay (the fallback when the emulator is unavailable) can start mid UTF-8 character or mid escape sequence and show garbage; trim to a safe boundary (found by bughunt) | 0017debb |

| M.ORCH-T1002 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | Bus state kinds can apply out of order: each StateBus send is its own connection and 4 inbox listeners relay concurrently (StatusInbox.cs:47), the hub retains without comparing (AppBusHub.cs:141-146) and StatePayload.AtUtc is never compared (MainViewModel.State.cs:24-56), so a quick pause on/off or two settings saves can leave the older value retained and applied everywhere (found by bughunt) | 503bab35 |
| M.ORCH-T1003 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | CapByStopHeadroom paces against a hard-coded 99% stop (StatusAggregator.cs:447 and AccountPacer.cs:140 pass PaceLedger.TargetPercent) instead of the real stop (PaceTargetPercent default 98, a member's 5-hour cutoff, or the weekly ceiling), overestimating headroom (at a 90% stop and 84% used it allows 5 subagents instead of 2), the burst M.ORCH-T959 meant to prevent (found by bughunt) | 9aa578be |
| M.ORCH-T1004 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | The context gate's take_nudges (AgentGate.cs:2797-2810) deletes nudge files it holds back while the stop holds, so for an unpaced (API-key) CLI or a CONTROL or exempt prompt at the stop, /allocate claim and resume nudges are silently lost; leave held nudges in place (found by bughunt) | 842ad0b2 |

| M.ORCH-T1006 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | The busy gate misclassifies CLIs: HostAncestor walks parent pids without start-time checks (BusyClis.cs:59-65, ProcessTree.cs:29-39), so an unhosted CLI whose dead parent's pid was reused by a TermHost counts as hosted and is cut off by an install; and unreadable state files or subagent marks with no CLI count as unknown even for hosted CLIs, refusing deploys for nothing (found by bughunt) | 79ee29af |

| M.ORCH-T1008 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | deploy.ps1 Get-NewestInstalled (line 177) indexes the dash split result [1] on a version folder without a build stamp (e.g. 1.0.0, which the regex and TermHostInstalls.Parse accept), which under Set-StrictMode Latest and ErrorActionPreference Stop aborts the whole deploy (found by bughunt) | c265d4b3 |
| M.ORCH-T1009 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | The daemon tick's three *Installs.Cleanup calls (Daemon.cs:144-153) are not wrapped in their own try, unlike the gateway's, so an exception there skips the rest of the tick (allocate, reminders, orphans, keep-going) and cleanup is not retried for 30 minutes because the timestamp is set first (found by bughunt) | 8594bf5b |

(landed on main since the last green run: tickets M.ORCH-T982, M.ORCH-T980, M.ORCH-T981, M.ORCH-T983, M.ORCH-T984, M.ORCH-T985, M.ORCH-T988, M.ORCH-T987, M.ORCH-T986, M.ORCH-T990, M.ORCH-T989, M.ORCH-T1010, M.ORCH-T1009, M.ORCH-T1008, M.ORCH-T1007, M.ORCH-T1006, M.ORCH-T1005, M.ORCH-T1004, M.ORCH-T1003, M.ORCH-T1002 in ec3663ae Mask secrets that arrive wrapped or slowly on remote streams: StreamMasker missed a token hard-wrapped by an Ink CLI with a real line break, split at a chunk boundary, or flushed by the 40ms quiet spell before it was long enough to match. Matching now also runs with a wrap's break (and indent) taken out, a trailing candidate (a begun shape past its prefix, a value after a secret-sounding name, the start of a Vault value) is held across line breaks and flushes until it can't be one, at most 500ms, then its secret part is masked rather than sent bare; the masker times its own holds (DueIn, FlushDue), a Title frame no longer pushes a held candidate out and other frames flush it masked, and ordinary text is never held longer than before (M.ORCH-T982); dbc36fa3 Mask secrets inside OSC, DCS and APC strings on remote streams: StreamMasker copied every escape sequence byte for byte, so a token in an OSC 0/2 title, an OSC 8 hyperlink, a DCS or APC string reached remote viewers unmasked in Output and Replay; now a string sequence's payload is masked on its own, introducer and terminator kept, and an OSC 52 clipboard write is decoded and dropped whole when it would copy a secret or can't be decoded (M.ORCH-T980); a388cb27 Mask session titles on the gateway's GET /sessions and freeze them while a session is paused: the listing ran the raw live title past the masker and kept updating it through a pause, so a secret in a title reached every watcher (the team wall polls every 10s); now it is masked as the stream is, and while paused the title listed before the pause is shown, never one set during it (M.ORCH-T981); 12ed6105 Close gateway streams whose token lapses: each stream's watch loop now re-validates its bearer token (held in memory, never logged) every interval as well as its grant, so a 15-minute token no longer keeps a stream open indefinitely; the serving gateway reads signing.key again when it changes (SigningKeyFile, keeping the old key over a transient read failure rather than minting a new one), so replacing it revokes every token, open streams included, without a restart (M.ORCH-T983); 2dc6057d Keep the gateway's per-stream revocation watch running through a failed check, and fail closed: the catch now sits inside the loop, so one throw from AccessTo no longer ends revocation checks and input auditing for the stream, and two failures running close it as revoked; AclGrants also skips null members, logins and grants in acl.json rather than throwing (M.ORCH-T984); 70583441 Refuse a member's remote attach to a protocol-1 TermHost on the gateway itself: a single-viewer host would drop its owner's own tab to serve the viewer, and only the team wall checked that client-side, so anyone in the org could keep kicking the owner off; now anyone but the owner gets 409 and a refused audit record (single-viewer host) before the pipe is opened (M.ORCH-T985); f9e7b79a Audit the gateway's unauthenticated refusals: a missing, bad or expired token on GET /sessions or a stream, and a wrong owner key on POST /auth/token, now each leave a refused term_audit record (viewer ?, level none, the session id when there is one, the reason in words, never the token, key or header), at most 60 a minute so a scanner can't flood the spool, the next one written saying how many were left out (M.ORCH-T988); df6d6b21 Bound the gateway's login throttle and make it O(1) and race-safe: one short lock, each address keeps only its last five failure times, at most 4096 addresses with the longest-quiet one forgotten first, an IPv6 address counted by its /64, and POST /auth/token counts an attempt before checking the key (TryBegin) and takes it back on success, so a flood of addresses can't grow memory or make every failure scan the table, and concurrent guesses can't slip past the five-try limit (M.ORCH-T987); 382c05a9 Keep the gateway's last good acl.json and broadcast.json when a read fails just now, and retry: TermGatewayAudit.TryReadAcl and TermBroadcast.TryRead tell a transient I/O failure from a missing or invalid file, AclGrants and BroadcastFile take the new stamp only once a read succeeds, and TermBroadcast.Update never writes a change over settings it couldn't read, so one sharing violation no longer locks members out or unshares every session until the file next changes (M.ORCH-T986); 844a503b Clean the viewer-supplied ViewerId before it reaches a log line: TermProtocol.LogSafeId drops control and format characters and caps it at 64 characters, TermHost logs only that, and the gateway forwards a remote viewer's Hello with its id cleaned, so no viewer can forge host log lines with embedded newlines (M.ORCH-T990); c7259581 Make orchestrator gateway revoke --session match the session id in any case, as the gateway does: grants store the id in lower case, and revoke compares LOWER(session), so a revoke typed in another case no longer reports no such grant while it stays in force (M.ORCH-T989); 62a49020 Judge an app presence by its pid and that process's start time against when the presence was said, not by pid alone: a presence the hub kept from an app long gone no longer counts once its pid is reused by a later process, so open-ticket starts Tickets.Desktop instead of going to nobody; one with no time of its own is still judged by pid (M.ORCH-T1010); 8594bf5b Contain each of the daemon tick's side-by-side cleanups (TermHost, Gateway, TermViewer) in its own try, as the gateway's tick is: one that throws no longer skips the rest of the tick (allocate, reminders, orphans, keep-going), and a failed cleanup is tried again in 5 minutes instead of waiting out the 30 the timestamp set first (M.ORCH-T1009); c265d4b3 Make deploy.ps1's Get-NewestInstalled safe under strict mode: a version folder with no build stamp (1.0.0, which its pattern and TermHostInstalls.Parse accept) now sorts by an empty stamp instead of indexing a missing [1] of the split, which threw under Set-StrictMode Latest and ErrorActionPreference Stop and aborted the whole deploy (M.ORCH-T1008); a090d88a Run deploy.ps1's busy gate before any install step: the CLI is now published to Cli.staging and swapped in only after the gate (the staged orchestrator.exe answers it), and the TermHost, Gateway and TermViewer are installed after it too, so a refused deploy installs nothing and no new CLI or host runs against the old daemon and dashboard (M.ORCH-T1007); 79ee29af Stop the busy gate misclassifying CLIs: the walk up to a TermHost now checks each step's start time and ends at a parent that started after its child (a dead parent's pid reused, say by a TermHost) or whose start can't be read, so an unhosted CLI is no longer taken for hosted and cut off by an install; and an unreadable state file or a subagent mark naming no CLI no longer refuses a deploy while every open CLI is hosted, since it can only be one of theirs (M.ORCH-T1006); 3d3c9119 Keep the Stop hook inside its 60s timeout and save the turn's idle state first: the context gate now counts a 45s budget from its start, gives `orchestrator next` only what's left of it (at most 30s, none under 3s), skips the ticket database and the workspace scan when the budget is nearly spent, and saves the session as idle before any of those slow asks, so a hook killed at its timeout no longer leaves the busy gate and the dashboard thinking the CLI is working (M.ORCH-T1005); 842ad0b2 Leave held nudges in place: the context gate's take_nudges deleted every nudge file it held back while the window's stop held, so an unpaced (API-key) CLI's, or one whose CONTROL or exempt prompt ran at the stop, lost its /allocate claim and resume nudges unread; now a held nudge stays for a later hook and only a stale one is dropped (M.ORCH-T1004); 9aa578be Measure CapByStopHeadroom's room to the login's real 5-hour stop instead of a hard-coded 99%: Pacer.StopPercent takes the lowest of the hooks' stop, the pace target the settings carry (PaceTargetPercent, 98 by default, with a member's own 5-hour cutoff laid over it) and the weekly ceiling while the week caps the window, at full double precision, so at a 90% stop and 84% used 2 subagents start, not 5 (M.ORCH-T1003); 503bab35 Apply and keep a bus state kind (members, orgs, settings, pause, reminders) only when its payload's AtUtc is no older than the one held: the daemon's hub drops an older own-store message instead of retaining and relaying it, and the dashboard drops one older than the last of its kind it applied, so a quick pause on/off or two settings saves arriving out of order no longer leave the older value in force (M.ORCH-T1002)) | passes on main@7f8f038 |

c265d4b3 Make deploy.ps1's Get-NewestInstalled safe under strict mode: a version folder with no build stamp (1.0.0, which its pattern and TermHostInstalls.Parse accept) now sorts by an empty stamp instead of indexing a missing [1] of the split, which threw under Set-StrictMode Latest and ErrorActionPreference Stop and aborted the whole deploy (M.ORCH-T1008); a090d88a Run deploy.ps1's busy gate before any install step: the CLI is now published to Cli.staging and swapped in only after the gate (the staged orchestrator.exe answers it), and the TermHost, Gateway and TermViewer are installed after it too, so a refused deploy installs nothing and no new CLI or host runs against the old daemon and dashboard (M.ORCH-T1007); 79ee29af Stop the busy gate misclassifying CLIs: the walk up to a TermHost now checks each step's start time and ends at a parent that started after its child (a dead parent's pid reused, say by a TermHost) or whose start can't be read, so an unhosted CLI is no longer taken for hosted and cut off by an install; and an unreadable state file or a subagent mark naming no CLI no longer refuses a deploy while every open CLI is hosted, since it can only be one of theirs (M.ORCH-T1006); 3d3c9119 Keep the Stop hook inside its 60s timeout and save the turn's idle state first: the context gate now counts a 45s budget from its start, gives `orchestrator next` only what's left of it (at most 30s, none under 3s), skips the ticket database and the workspace scan when the budget is nearly spent, and saves the session as idle before any of those slow asks, so a hook killed at its timeout no longer leaves the busy gate and the dashboard thinking the CLI is working (M.ORCH-T1005); 842ad0b2 Leave held nudges in place: the context gate's take_nudges deleted every nudge file it held back while the window's stop held, so an unpaced (API-key) CLI's, or one whose CONTROL or exempt prompt ran at the stop, lost its /allocate claim and resume nudges unread; now a held nudge stays for a later hook and only a stale one is dropped (M.ORCH-T1004); 9aa578be Measure CapByStopHeadroom's room to the login's real 5-hour stop instead of a hard-coded 99%: Pacer.StopPercent takes the lowest of the hooks' stop, the pace target the settings carry (PaceTargetPercent, 98 by default, with a member's own 5-hour cutoff laid over it) and the weekly ceiling while the week caps the window, at full double precision, so at a 90% stop and 84% used 2 subagents start, not 5 (M.ORCH-T1003); 503bab35 Apply and keep a bus state kind (members, orgs, settings, pause, reminders) only when its payload's AtUtc is no older than the one held: the daemon's hub drops an older own-store message instead of retaining and relaying it, and the dashboard drops one older than the last of its kind it applied, so a quick pause on/off or two settings saves arriving out of order no longer leave the older value in force (M.ORCH-T1002)) | passes on main@1ff7a42 |

eb646ec6 Stop hook: save the turn as still busy with a deciding mark, not idle, before deciding whether to send it on, and idle only when the turn really ends, so an /allocate CLI about to continue no longer reads idle to a deploy's busy gate or a restart gate for up to 45 s; 00b8510a BusyClis: keep the unknowns (a subagent mark naming no CLI, an unreadable state) even when every CLI the scan found is hosted, dropping an unreadable state only when its session is provably a hosted or the asking CLI's, so an unhosted CLI the process scan missed refuses a deploy again (M.ORCH-T1042); b6454c28 deploy.ps1: count src/MindAttic.Orchestrator.Term in the dashboard's and the CLI's change detection, since Core references it, so a Term-only change redeploys them along with TermHost and Gateway instead of leaving them on the old Term code (M.ORCH-T1031); 3235fcb7 --install: start the dashboard again when the install stopped a running one, so a deploy without -Launch no longer leaves it down with every hosted CLI in a fallback TermViewer and its restore file waiting for an upgrade restart; 59e58745 TermBus: track the retries of sends that missed and wait for them, bounded (6 s), before a TermHost exits after its ended announcement and before the gateway exits after its watcher reset, so neither final message is lost with the process (M.ORCH-T1017); 0363c38d AppBusHub: check a state payload is newer and publish it under one lock, so an older payload checked first can no longer be published after a newer one and stay retained (M.ORCH-T1013); ec3663ae Mask secrets that arrive wrapped or slowly on remote streams: StreamMasker missed a token hard-wrapped by an Ink CLI with a real line break, split at a chunk boundary, or flushed by the 40ms quiet spell before it was long enough to match. Matching now also runs with a wrap's break (and indent) taken out, a trailing candidate (a begun shape past its prefix, a value after a secret-sounding name, the start of a Vault value) is held across line breaks and flushes until it can't be one, at most 500ms, then its secret part is masked rather than sent bare; the masker times its own holds (DueIn, FlushDue), a Title frame no longer pushes a held candidate out and other frames flush it masked, and ordinary text is never held longer than before (M.ORCH-T982); dbc36fa3 Mask secrets inside OSC, DCS and APC strings on remote streams: StreamMasker copied every escape sequence byte for byte, so a token in an OSC 0/2 title, an OSC 8 hyperlink, a DCS or APC string reached remote viewers unmasked in Output and Replay; now a string sequence's payload is masked on its own, introducer and terminator kept, and an OSC 52 clipboard write is decoded and dropped whole when it would copy a secret or can't be decoded (M.ORCH-T980); a388cb27 Mask session titles on the gateway's GET /sessions and freeze them while a session is paused: the listing ran the raw live title past the masker and kept updating it through a pause, so a secret in a title reached every watcher (the team wall polls every 10s); now it is masked as the stream is, and while paused the title listed before the pause is shown, never one set during it (M.ORCH-T981); 12ed6105 Close gateway streams whose token lapses: each stream's watch loop now re-validates its bearer token (held in memory, never logged) every interval as well as its grant, so a 15-minute token no longer keeps a stream open indefinitely; the serving gateway reads signing.key again when it changes (SigningKeyFile, keeping the old key over a transient read failure rather than minting a new one), so replacing it revokes every token, open streams included, without a restart (M.ORCH-T983); 2dc6057d Keep the gateway's per-stream revocation watch running through a failed check, and fail closed: the catch now sits inside the loop, so one throw from AccessTo no longer ends revocation checks and input auditing for the stream, and two failures running close it as revoked; AclGrants also skips null members, logins and grants in acl.json rather than throwing (M.ORCH-T984); 70583441 Refuse a member's remote attach to a protocol-1 TermHost on the gateway itself: a single-viewer host would drop its owner's own tab to serve the viewer, and only the team wall checked that client-side, so anyone in the org could keep kicking the owner off; now anyone but the owner gets 409 and a refused audit record (single-viewer host) before the pipe is opened (M.ORCH-T985); f9e7b79a Audit the gateway's unauthenticated refusals: a missing, bad or expired token on GET /sessions or a stream, and a wrong owner key on POST /auth/token, now each leave a refused term_audit record (viewer ?, level none, the session id when there is one, the reason in words, never the token, key or header), at most 60 a minute so a scanner can't flood the spool, the next one written saying how many were left out (M.ORCH-T988); df6d6b21 Bound the gateway's login throttle and make it O(1) and race-safe: one short lock, each address keeps only its last five failure times, at most 4096 addresses with the longest-quiet one forgotten first, an IPv6 address counted by its /64, and POST /auth/token counts an attempt before checking the key (TryBegin) and takes it back on success, so a flood of addresses can't grow memory or make every failure scan the table, and concurrent guesses can't slip past the five-try limit (M.ORCH-T987)) | 359eaffdd0e0c02241dbaf39d8dbb30f3c9448df |

(landed on main since the last green run: tickets M.ORCH-T1041, M.ORCH-T1039, M.ORCH-T1038, M.ORCH-T1016, M.ORCH-T1028, M.ORCH-T1040, M.ORCH-T1035, M.ORCH-T1034, M.ORCH-T1033, M.ORCH-T1027, M.ORCH-T1026, M.ORCH-T1025, M.ORCH-T1024, M.ORCH-T1023, M.ORCH-T1022, M.ORCH-T1021, M.ORCH-T1032, M.ORCH-T1020, M.ORCH-T1019, M.ORCH-T1015 in cb7b7e3d Let a remote stream outlive its token with an in-band refresh: since T983 every gateway stream was cut when its bearer token expired and audited as "access revoked", since a WebSocket can't present a new token. A viewer may now send a RefreshToken frame (0x20, never forwarded to a host) carrying a fresh token; the gateway validates it as it did the attach token (signature, lifetime, the same member, at least the stream's access), and the stream then lasts as long as it does; refused ones are logged and audited (at most five per stream). A lapse is closed and audited as "token expired"; a replaced signing key still closes the stream at the next check as "access revoked". The team wall's and the pop-out viewer's streams (WebSocketFrameStream via GatewayClient) look at the member's token in the settings every 20s and send any newer one for the same gateway, so a token renewed with gateway remote add keeps open tiles running (M.ORCH-T1041); 34668fed Close two remote-stream masking gaps left by T982: a Replay was masked with final:true, so a token half-printed when a viewer attached went out bare up to the replay's end; it is now masked as a held candidate whose hold ran out (StreamMasker.ProcessReplay), and the rest of it masked as live output goes on. And once a held candidate's start was masked, a short value (a password after password:) that then failed the 16-character LooksRandom test stopped being a candidate and its remainder went out bare; a run whose start was masked unfinished is now masked to its end, across a wrap's break, and no further (M.ORCH-T1039); 31a875e0 Stop the remote-stream masker bulleting ordinary code: since T982 any value after key/token/secret/password with one digit or capital (key=1, apiKey = getT) or the first 8 characters of a Vault value was a candidate, masked for good once its 500ms hold ran out or on any non-Output frame, such as the frequent Modes frames. Candidates are now weak or strong: key=1 and other short digit runs aren't held at all; a code-like value and a Vault value's first few characters are only held, in case the rest makes a match, then sent as they are; only a begun token shape, a value after a password name, a value after another name of 8+ characters with digits and letters, or 12+ characters (or half) of a Vault value is masked unfinished. Modes, Size and other non-content frames now pass a held candidate as a Title does; only Exit flushes it (M.ORCH-T1038); 226b4522 Close the session pipe when the gateway's WebSocket upgrade fails: the pipe opened for a stream was disposed only inside TermBridge.RunAsync, so an AcceptWebSocketAsync that threw left it open, leaking a handle per failed upgrade and a half-open viewer on the host; it is now disposed before the failure goes on to the contained 500 (M.ORCH-T1016); 2e7a87b7 Restart the team gateway onto a newer install after a redeploy: GatewaySupervisor kept a managed gateway running for as long as its settings matched, so an old build (say, one whose masker leaks secrets) kept serving remote viewers and its version folder was never cleaned up. The gateway's status now names its exe; each tick the supervisor compares it (or, for an older gateway, its process's main module, then its version) with the exe it would start now, the newest under GatewayInstalls, and restarts it there when they differ; remote viewers reconnect (M.ORCH-T1028); a38adcd4 Let fallback TermViewer windows reconnect while the dashboard is absent: since T976 they got no liveness probe, so a passing pipe drop with the dashboard down left the window detached, holding the slot mutex and dropping keys. They now reconnect while the host lives and the dashboard's presence hasn't been seen; once it is, the probe says no and the window folds as before (M.ORCH-T1040); a46d5294 Treat a registry read failure as unknown, not gone, when a dropped relay asks whether its host lives: TermSessions.Get returned null when a read failed, so a passing antivirus or indexer hold marked the tab ended for good (and closing it killed a live CLI). TermSessions.TryGet tells the two apart, as Enumerate does since T995, and HostAlive then asks the host's process (M.ORCH-T1035); 1f572d64 Report a failed kill and keep its tab: TermHostKill swallowed a kill that failed (an elevated host), so the tab went while the host lived and the resync re-added it later. Kill now says whether the host is gone; a tab close that couldn't end it keeps the tab with a toast, End CLI keeps the viewer with a status, and a Started message for a session closed here lately no longer gets a tab back (M.ORCH-T1034); 03b6ae72 Unregister a killed host from the killer: closing a tab or End CLI hard-kills the host tree, so Registration.End never ran, no ended went on the bus and the registry file lingered until a reader pruned it. After a successful kill TermHostKill now waits (off the caller's thread, up to 2s) for the host to go, deletes its registry file and announces ended (M.ORCH-T1033); d1296b2d Collapse the API credit burndown card until there is a spend reading, as the utilization card does: the API-key tab showed a blank card with a null chart and an accessible name ending in a bare colon (M.ORCH-T1027); 1ca0c44a Name the CLI tab's shared glyph for screen readers: TerminalSharedGlyph had only a tooltip, so a screen reader read a private-use glyph and the shared state was lost; it gets an AutomationProperties.Name like its watched sibling (M.ORCH-T1026); 798638ca Bring the selected person tab into view: the horizontally scrolled login strip never followed the selection, so Ctrl+Tab, Show who's working or an org switch could select a tab left off screen. The selected tab's container is brought into view after each selection or strip change (M.ORCH-T1025); f71c811f Tell the CLI tab strip its selection stands after a Ctrl+click: PersonTerminalsViewModel.SelectedPane ignored the null write without raising PropertyChanged, so the strip showed nothing chosen while the terminal stayed shown. It now re-raises once the binding's write is done; the login tab strip's StripSelection does the same (M.ORCH-T1024); 2d943eef Show the global tab's Tickets section even when its login's email is unknown: in an API-key-only setup ShowsUserTickets required PersonEmail, hiding the queue tabs and the only unassigned queue (M.ORCH-T1023); 7ded8fb4 Put Show who's working replies on the shown tab's status line: ShowWorker set the global tab's StatusMessage, but the toolbar binds and announces the shown tab's, so Nobody is working X and the like never appeared with a person tab shown (M.ORCH-T1022); 47709d7f Make the team wall keyboard and screen-reader usable: its flat buttons (Watch, Interact, page, Refresh) were Focusable=false and nameless, so nothing could be paged, refreshed or opened without a mouse. They take focus now, each with a name (per tile for Watch/Interact) and help text, tiles are named by person and title, and the page counter reads as Page n of m (M.ORCH-T1021); 1c7903a7 Gate the team wall's tile pop-out by host protocol, as the dashboard's menu is: a protocol 1 host serves one viewer, so popping one out made the pop-out and the owner's tab take the session from each other in a reconnect loop. TeamWall.CanPopOut (Streamable) gates PopOut and the tile says why (M.ORCH-T1032); a3f17c4e Let the terminal frame shrink: its fixed 480 in an Auto row starved the only star row, so below ~700px or zoomed in the stats, queue tabs, chart and tickets became unreachable. While shown its row is now 3* capped at 480 (frame MinHeight 160) and the body keeps MinHeight 120 (M.ORCH-T1020); 7dc6fd0b Deselect the login tab strip before emptying it: switching to an org with no Claude login removed the still-selected tab from the bound strip (the T859 crash). The strip now binds StripSelection, which reads null while SyncOrgTabs empties it, and the window keeps showing the tab (M.ORCH-T1019); ecdad566 Coalesce relay output into the UI thread and bound it: output raised while a batch is waiting joins it (one posted closure per UI turn, not per frame; any other event seals the batch so order holds), and past 1M pending chars the reader stops reading the link until the UI drains half, so the host's per-viewer cap applies (M.ORCH-T1015)) | passes on main@bccf033 |

They take focus now, each with a name (per tile for Watch/Interact) and help text, tiles are named by person and title, and the page counter reads as Page n of m (M.ORCH-T1021); 1c7903a7 Gate the team wall's tile pop-out by host protocol, as the dashboard's menu is: a protocol 1 host serves one viewer, so popping one out made the pop-out and the owner's tab take the session from each other in a reconnect loop. TeamWall.CanPopOut (Streamable) gates PopOut and the tile says why (M.ORCH-T1032); a3f17c4e Let the terminal frame shrink: its fixed 480 in an Auto row starved the only star row, so below ~700px or zoomed in the stats, queue tabs, chart and tickets became unreachable. While shown its row is now 3* capped at 480 (frame MinHeight 160) and the body keeps MinHeight 120 (M.ORCH-T1020); 7dc6fd0b Deselect the login tab strip before emptying it: switching to an org with no Claude login removed the still-selected tab from the bound strip (the T859 crash). The strip now binds StripSelection, which reads null while SyncOrgTabs empties it, and the window keeps showing the tab (M.ORCH-T1019); ecdad566 Coalesce relay output into the UI thread and bound it: output raised while a batch is waiting joins it (one posted closure per UI turn, not per frame; any other event seals the batch so order holds), and past 1M pending chars the reader stops reading the link until the UI drains half, so the host's per-viewer cap applies (M.ORCH-T1015)) | passes on main@1ff7a42 |
| M.ORCH-T1055 | 2026-10-26 | fix | closed | Fails on main: MindAttic.Orchestrator.Tests.GatewayTests.A_revoked_grant_closes_the_stream_it_allowed — System.OperationCanceledException : The operation was canceled. (landed on main since the last green run: tickets M.ORCH-T1052, M.ORCH-T1050, M.ORCH-T1049, M.ORCH-T1048, M.ORCH-T1041, M.ORCH-T1039, M.ORCH-T1038, M.ORCH-T1016, M.ORCH-T1028, M.ORCH-T1040, M.ORCH-T1035, M.ORCH-T1034, M.ORCH-T1033, M.ORCH-T1027, M.ORCH-T1026, M.ORCH-T1025, M.ORCH-T1024, M.ORCH-T1023, M.ORCH-T1022, M.ORCH-T1021 in 607e1905 Guard the context gate's PostToolUse state save so a failed write can't raise a hook error on a CLI's tool call (M.ORCH-T1052); 9babfeba Fold a fallback TermViewer at once when its link is replaced while the dashboard is present: since T1040 it stopped reconnecting only once dashboardSeen was set (two presence looks, 2-4s, or a bus presence), so a dashboard reattaching to a protocol-1 host first ping-ponged the single-viewer session with it for a few seconds. Its reconnect probe and OnDetached now also look at DashboardPresence.IsPresent (the dashboard's single-instance mutex or show event exists) and fold (M.ORCH-T1050); e70dc9f3 Never send the start of a Vault value bare: since T1038 a Vault value's first 8-11 characters were a weak masker candidate, sent as they were after their 500ms hold or at a flush, so a real secret printed with a gap leaked up to half of itself to remote viewers. Any held start of a Vault value is now strong, masked when its hold runs out, at a flush, and even by a final call; weak candidates such as apiKey = getT still go as they are (M.ORCH-T1049); 5c99472a Let a Stop hook cut off after its deciding save read idle to every reader: ContextCycler.Read now applies the 75s deciding-staleness rule (IsBusyTurn) as BusyClis and LiveSessions do, so AllocateWaker, Allocate.ByHand and LimitWaker no longer see that CLI working for good; the hook pops deciding in its PostToolUse and Notification saves, and its final save can no longer raise (M.ORCH-T1048); cb7b7e3d Let a remote stream outlive its token with an in-band refresh: since T983 every gateway stream was cut when its bearer token expired and audited as "access revoked", since a WebSocket can't present a new token. A viewer may now send a RefreshToken frame (0x20, never forwarded to a host) carrying a fresh token; the gateway validates it as it did the attach token (signature, lifetime, the same member, at least the stream's access), and the stream then lasts as long as it does; refused ones are logged and audited (at most five per stream). A lapse is closed and audited as "token expired"; a replaced signing key still closes the stream at the next check as "access revoked". The team wall's and the pop-out viewer's streams (WebSocketFrameStream via GatewayClient) look at the member's token in the settings every 20s and send any newer one for the same gateway, so a token renewed with gateway remote add keeps open tiles running (M.ORCH-T1041); 34668fed Close two remote-stream masking gaps left by T982: a Replay was masked with final:true, so a token half-printed when a viewer attached went out bare up to the replay's end; it is now masked as a held candidate whose hold ran out (StreamMasker.ProcessReplay), and the rest of it masked as live output goes on. And once a held candidate's start was masked, a short value (a password after password:) that then failed the 16-character LooksRandom test stopped being a candidate and its remainder went out bare; a run whose start was masked unfinished is now masked to its end, across a wrap's break, and no further (M.ORCH-T1039); 31a875e0 Stop the remote-stream masker bulleting ordinary code: since T982 any value after key/token/secret/password with one digit or capital (key=1, apiKey = getT) or the first 8 characters of a Vault value was a candidate, masked for good once its 500ms hold ran out or on any non-Output frame, such as the frequent Modes frames. Candidates are now weak or strong: key=1 and other short digit runs aren't held at all; a code-like value and a Vault value's first few characters are only held, in case the rest makes a match, then sent as they are; only a begun token shape, a value after a password name, a value after another name of 8+ characters with digits and letters, or 12+ characters (or half) of a Vault value is masked unfinished. Modes, Size and other non-content frames now pass a held candidate as a Title does; only Exit flushes it (M.ORCH-T1038); 226b4522 Close the session pipe when the gateway's WebSocket upgrade fails: the pipe opened for a stream was disposed only inside TermBridge.RunAsync, so an AcceptWebSocketAsync that threw left it open, leaking a handle per failed upgrade and a half-open viewer on the host; it is now disposed before the failure goes on to the contained 500 (M.ORCH-T1016); 2e7a87b7 Restart the team gateway onto a newer install after a redeploy: GatewaySupervisor kept a managed gateway running for as long as its settings matched, so an old build (say, one whose masker leaks secrets) kept serving remote viewers and its version folder was never cleaned up. The gateway's status now names its exe; each tick the supervisor compares it (or, for an older gateway, its process's main module, then its version) with the exe it would start now, the newest under GatewayInstalls, and restarts it there when they differ; remote viewers reconnect (M.ORCH-T1028); a38adcd4 Let fallback TermViewer windows reconnect while the dashboard is absent: since T976 they got no liveness probe, so a passing pipe drop with the dashboard down left the window detached, holding the slot mutex and dropping keys. They now reconnect while the host lives and the dashboard's presence hasn't been seen; once it is, the probe says no and the window folds as before (M.ORCH-T1040); a46d5294 Treat a registry read failure as unknown, not gone, when a dropped relay asks whether its host lives: TermSessions.Get returned null when a read failed, so a passing antivirus or indexer hold marked the tab ended for good (and closing it killed a live CLI). TermSessions.TryGet tells the two apart, as Enumerate does since T995, and HostAlive then asks the host's process (M.ORCH-T1035); 1f572d64 Report a failed kill and keep its tab: TermHostKill swallowed a kill that failed (an elevated host), so the tab went while the host lived and the resync re-added it later. Kill now says whether the host is gone; a tab close that couldn't end it keeps the tab with a toast, End CLI keeps the viewer with a status, and a Started message for a session closed here lately no longer gets a tab back (M.ORCH-T1034); 03b6ae72 Unregister a killed host from the killer: closing a tab or End CLI hard-kills the host tree, so Registration.End never ran, no ended went on the bus and the registry file lingered until a reader pruned it. After a successful kill TermHostKill now waits (off the caller's thread, up to 2s) for the host to go, deletes its registry file and announces ended (M.ORCH-T1033); d1296b2d Collapse the API credit burndown card until there is a spend reading, as the utilization card does: the API-key tab showed a blank card with a null chart and an accessible name ending in a bare colon (M.ORCH-T1027); 1ca0c44a Name the CLI tab's shared glyph for screen readers: TerminalSharedGlyph had only a tooltip, so a screen reader read a private-use glyph and the shared state was lost; it gets an AutomationProperties.Name like its watched sibling (M.ORCH-T1026); 798638ca Bring the selected person tab into view: the horizontally scrolled login strip never followed the selection, so Ctrl+Tab, Show who's working or an org switch could select a tab left off screen. The selected tab's container is brought into view after each selection or strip change (M.ORCH-T1025); f71c811f Tell the CLI tab strip its selection stands after a Ctrl+click: PersonTerminalsViewModel.SelectedPane ignored the null write without raising PropertyChanged, so the strip showed nothing chosen while the terminal stayed shown. It now re-raises once the binding's write is done; the login tab strip's StripSelection does the same (M.ORCH-T1024); 2d943eef Show the global tab's Tickets section even when its login's email is unknown: in an API-key-only setup ShowsUserTickets required PersonEmail, hiding the queue tabs and the only unassigned queue (M.ORCH-T1023); 7ded8fb4 Put Show who's working replies on the shown tab's status line: ShowWorker set the global tab's StatusMessage, but the toolbar binds and announces the shown tab's, so Nobody is working X and the like never appeared with a person tab shown (M.ORCH-T1022); 47709d7f Make the team wall keyboard and screen-reader usable: its flat buttons (Watch, Interact, page, Refresh) were Focusable=false and nameless, so nothing could be paged, refreshed or opened without a mouse. They take focus now, each with a name (per tile for Watch/Interact) and help text, tiles are named by person and title, and the page counter reads as Page n of m (M.ORCH-T1021)) | passes on main@bccf033 |

Any held start of a Vault value is now strong, masked when its hold runs out, at a flush, and even by a final call; weak candidates such as apiKey = getT still go as they are (M.ORCH-T1049); 5c99472a Let a Stop hook cut off after its deciding save read idle to every reader: ContextCycler.Read now applies the 75s deciding-staleness rule (IsBusyTurn) as BusyClis and LiveSessions do, so AllocateWaker, Allocate.ByHand and LimitWaker no longer see that CLI working for good; the hook pops deciding in its PostToolUse and Notification saves, and its final save can no longer raise (M.ORCH-T1048); cb7b7e3d Let a remote stream outlive its token with an in-band refresh: since T983 every gateway stream was cut when its bearer token expired and audited as "access revoked", since a WebSocket can't present a new token. A viewer may now send a RefreshToken frame (0x20, never forwarded to a host) carrying a fresh token; the gateway validates it as it did the attach token (signature, lifetime, the same member, at least the stream's access), and the stream then lasts as long as it does; refused ones are logged and audited (at most five per stream). A lapse is closed and audited as "token expired"; a replaced signing key still closes the stream at the next check as "access revoked". The team wall's and the pop-out viewer's streams (WebSocketFrameStream via GatewayClient) look at the member's token in the settings every 20s and send any newer one for the same gateway, so a token renewed with gateway remote add keeps open tiles running (M.ORCH-T1041); 34668fed Close two remote-stream masking gaps left by T982: a Replay was masked with final:true, so a token half-printed when a viewer attached went out bare up to the replay's end; it is now masked as a held candidate whose hold ran out (StreamMasker.ProcessReplay), and the rest of it masked as live output goes on. And once a held candidate's start was masked, a short value (a password after password:) that then failed the 16-character LooksRandom test stopped being a candidate and its remainder went out bare; a run whose start was masked unfinished is now masked to its end, across a wrap's break, and no further (M.ORCH-T1039); 31a875e0 Stop the remote-stream masker bulleting ordinary code: since T982 any value after key/token/secret/password with one digit or capital (key=1, apiKey = getT) or the first 8 characters of a Vault value was a candidate, masked for good once its 500ms hold ran out or on any non-Output frame, such as the frequent Modes frames. Candidates are now weak or strong: key=1 and other short digit runs aren't held at all; a code-like value and a Vault value's first few characters are only held, in case the rest makes a match, then sent as they are; only a begun token shape, a value after a password name, a value after another name of 8+ characters with digits and letters, or 12+ characters (or half) of a Vault value is masked unfinished. Modes, Size and other non-content frames now pass a held candidate as a Title does; only Exit flushes it (M.ORCH-T1038); 226b4522 Close the session pipe when the gateway's WebSocket upgrade fails: the pipe opened for a stream was disposed only inside TermBridge.RunAsync, so an AcceptWebSocketAsync that threw left it open, leaking a handle per failed upgrade and a half-open viewer on the host; it is now disposed before the failure goes on to the contained 500 (M.ORCH-T1016); 2e7a87b7 Restart the team gateway onto a newer install after a redeploy: GatewaySupervisor kept a managed gateway running for as long as its settings matched, so an old build (say, one whose masker leaks secrets) kept serving remote viewers and its version folder was never cleaned up. 6608db5f Remote host mode: a client PC's tickets commands run on the host through its gateway, the host shares every CLI with the PC's Team Wall, and setup-host.ps1 installs winget where there's no Store (M.ORCH-T1479); 92e8a4a8 Remote host mode: run the Orchestrator on a separate Windows 11 VM so it stops using the PC's memory; machine roles, one-command host setup, a self-renewing link to the PC (M.ORCH-T1473); 3e64f156 %TEMP%\claude session folders are deleted by liveness, never age: only when the session's CLI has definitely exited (read from every login's session-context, or no Claude CLI runs at all), no running process names the folder, no unconsumed handoff or running transcript points into it, and nothing in it is open; the 1-day "unknown and quiet" fallback, the 30-minute ended-quiet rule and the low-disk deletion of running sessions' scratch are gone, and disk-cleanup --dry-run lists every folder's verdict (M.ORCH-T1467); 452a5812 Wind down button: /allocate off and Pacing off for every CLI across every login at once (M.ORCH-T1468); 7267c0e0 Lower the default 5-hour pace target from 98% to 96% (M.ORCH-T1462); dbe4b006 UsageCutoffTests: the raised-cutoff test checked 93% against its own 88% warn line; check 85% (past org-wide 80, short of its own line) is Ok and 93% warns (M.ORCH-T1451); f31012b4 Claims nudge filter keeps the nudge when assignments can't be read and parses ids by pattern (M.ORCH-T1253); ac27a4c8 Stop hook and orchestrator next share one pace truth: nothing handed out or nudged while the cool-off abort would fire; stale claims dropped from nudges (M.ORCH-T1253); bcbaf6ab Gate returns the /crossrepo list directly when it names repos (M.ORCH-T1258); e093d5a6 Respect the /crossrepo list: intersect /allocate and next repos with it, and bound the edit and close gates by it (M.ORCH-T1258); 864030c4 Cli csproj finds the workspace from any <workspace>.worktrees\<repo>\<name> checkout (drops .worktrees), so the main-tests build resolves MindAttic.Helpers without run.ps1's MindAtticRoot (M.ORCH-T1310); 3b00084f Disk self-cleanup: new --disk-cleanup-gb setting (default 30, 0 off); under it the daemon tick (every 5 min max, off-thread), a 60s-cached free-space check in the generated context gate and `orchestrator disk-cleanup [--dry-run] [--quiet]` delete agent-made temp oldest first until line+10 GB: ended sessions' %TEMP%\claude folders (session-id folders only, never tasks output, 30 min quiet) and running sessions' stale big scratch (2h, 64 MB+); nothing written in 15 min, no worktrees, no non-agent files (page/hibernation file and other %TEMP% folders are only named); every deletion logged to data/disk-cleanup.log, alert with what it freed; DiskCleanupTests (M.ORCH-T1449)) | 553d68cd |

056bf031 Memory guard's last resort: while RAM is critical the daemon sheds the newest ticket subagent once a minute (never one landing, never a CLI or a manual session's subagents, nothing killed) through the cool-off's abort mark, which now says it's to free memory; the daemon's stepped level and lines count while fresh (M.ORCH-T1495); f3c06d74 Memory guard: low RAM holds new work like the 5-hour and weekly stops, so the machine never pages itself to a full disk. the daemon's stepped level and lines count while fresh (M.ORCH-T1495); f3c06d74 Memory guard: low RAM holds new work like the 5-hour and weekly stops, so the machine never pages itself to a full disk. 03489469 release.ps1 builds origin/main and bundles the Launcher and tickets, so a fresh PC needs no source build (M.ORCH-T1548); 974edb95 Welcome window fits a phone and hides a finished step's action row (M.ORCH-T1551); abeb37f2 release.ps1 packs the deployed Orchestrator into a downloadable zip; Welcome installs the .NET runtimes (M.ORCH-T1547); 4003fb0e Welcome window walks a new user from download to a signed-in dashboard (M.ORCH-T1545); 3aaecff9 Phone layout's mic and say box talk to the CLI (M.ORCH-T1544); 32acdfee Dashboard pivots to a phone layout when narrow or portrait (M.ORCH-T1543); 5c254b16 Hide the lambda/5-hour bar for solo Ultra logins on the tab strip and Usage tab (M.ORCH-T1540); 1e1d26da Bughunt: GatewayClient.RunTicketsAsync catches InvalidOperationException from a non-object JSON answer; OpenTicketSource.FromDatabase returns null (not []) on an unreadable-with-no-cache database read, so OpenFor falls back to the markdown instead of reading as zero tickets; ExportedState.Write and MachineRole.Save catch/avoid the same transient file-I/O races every sibling temp-file writer already does; DiffReview.RunClaude checks Task.WaitAll's own return value instead of silently reading an incomplete pipe as empty output (M.ORCH-T1539); 6309ad93 Bughunt: complete the dead refresh-timing Stopwatch in RefreshAsync (logs a Dashboard warning past 5s instead of being silently inert), and stop presumeTimer/notSentTimer/typingTimer in DisposeControl so a closed pane's timers don't fire SetPresumed/RaiseBadges/PresumptionChanged against it later (M.ORCH-T1538); 1e60ba6e Select() times a login tab switch and logs a Dashboard warning past 300ms, so a slow one (e.g. ~30s for one login, none of the others) leaves a number and a login name in the log instead of nothing (M.ORCH-T1537); 41b79392 Login tab bars right-aligned via MaTabItem.TrailingContent (MindAttic.Components.Wpf 32.0.0, M.COMP-T172) instead of living in the Header, where they only ever sat right after the name; the hover tooltip's first line is now the current Sigma/lambda percents (TabUsageLine), ahead of the bulleted cutoffs/reset/active-CLIs lines. Along the way, fixes the three test regressions M.ORCH-T1532 left on main: TerminalPanesTests expected the chart inline in AgentsBodyList (it now lives in its own UsageFrame), LibraryOnlyXamlTests flagged the ToolTipService.InitialShowDelay style setter (allowed now - timing, not a look), and TabStatusTests still expected the old Trailing={Binding TabTrailing} binding (M.ORCH-T1536) (M.ORCH-T1533) (M.ORCH-T1534) (M.ORCH-T1535); 4ee0dfec The pinned Usage tab opens its own page (UsageFrame, a sibling of TerminalFrame) holding the 5h/weekly charts, in place of just hiding the terminal and scrolling to where they used to sit inline; each login row shows the same weekly/5h bars beside its name instead of the plain percent text (the percents move to the tooltip, ShowsTabUsageBars/TabTrailingFace); the login tab's callout tooltip now opens instantly (ToolTipService.InitialShowDelay=0) (M.ORCH-T1532)) | passes on main@daa7138 |

6a0d9267 Bisect a red main line to the commit that broke it: a suite run that files new "Fails on main" tickets queues a bisect from the last green run to the red head in its own main-bisect worktree, sharing the one heavy slot with the suites and held by the memory guard, bounded by the MainBisectMaxSteps (8, 0 off) and MainBisectTimeoutMinutes (240) Vault settings with LampSettingsTests cases; cdac5826 Ledger sweeper: on daemon start and at the session-temp prune's cadence, reclaims resource-ledger entries whose owner is dead or finished (a ticket's scratch once it's closed with its commit on origin's main line or handed back, else when its lease runs out; a session's or process's once it's gone), crash leftovers in %TEMP% and stale bin/obj in the daemon's worktrees; dry run by default, logging what it would delete to disk-cleanup.log, with orchestrator disk-cleanup --ledger / --ledger-run (M.ORCH-T1677); 988fe028 Disk floor finished: the agent hook holds then refuses a new subagent under the floor as the memory guard's tight level does (live free-disk read against the daemon's lines, fails open), a CLI started by hand from the dashboard is refused with the reason, the menu bar shows the hold, and orchestrator branches test waits on disk as on RAM (BranchTestsDiskWaitMinutes, Vault) (M.ORCH-T1692); 3e7765f6 Growth caps, each a Vault setting: the hourly prune rotates disk-cleanup.log to .1..N past DiskCleanupLogMaxKb (1024, keeping DiskCleanupLogKeep 3); every DbMaintenanceHours (24) DbMaintenance age-prunes term_audit and gate_events past DbEventKeepDays (90), usage_history and ticket_costs only when DbHistoryKeepDays > 0 (default keeps them), and VACUUMs the SQLite file once DbVacuumMinFreePercent (20) of it is free pages (SQL Server never vacuumed or reconfigured); transcript retention is TranscriptKeepDays (default 365) written as each login's exact cleanupPeriodDays, 0 leaves it, and the daemon rewrites the hooks when it changes (M.ORCH-T1681); 0028930e Heavy-process lease, every number and the pattern list a Vault setting: HeavyProcessPatterns (extra heavy commands, JSON, added to the built-in list and the repo's .agent/heavy-patterns.json), HeavyProcessGraceSeconds (60), HeavyProcessUnknownMaxSeconds (900) and HeavyProcessSlackSeconds (5), read live by the pace gate's hook and by orchestrator clis, each with a LampSettingsTests case (M.ORCH-T1680); e7ed1557 HookScriptTests: the database-busy fallback test measures 'not stuck on the database' against a no-hold, free-database run of the same call instead of a fixed 25s, which a RAM-starved machine's python start alone exceeds; the hook's 3s DB budget is unchanged (M.ORCH-T1693); 6d004e03 Heavy-process lease: the pace gate makes a shell command that matches the heavy pattern list (Unity/Unreal/s&box builds and editors, built game players, soak runners; each new item is texted once through Psst, never repeated, behind the InboxAlerts setting (M.ORCH-T1689); c71959e4 Disk floor holds new work: under DiskHoldGb free (5 GB) the self-cleanup runs first, and if the drive is still under it allocate hands out nothing, no new CLI starts and main-line tests and branch builds wait, until it's DiskHoldResumeMarginGb clear; running work is never stopped (M.ORCH-T1679); 63904c0b Resource ledger: a resources table in orchestrator.db records every scratch dir, worktree and temp file the orchestrator creates with its owner and lease expiry, and each claimed ticket gets its own scratch dir passed to its agent as ORCH_SCRATCH (M.ORCH-T1676); 7b8cfe16 Bisect a red main line to the commit that broke it: new failures queue a bisect from the last green run in its own main-bisect worktree (one heavy slot with the suites, held by the memory guard, bounded by the MainBisectMaxSteps/MainBisectTimeoutMinutes Vault settings with LampSettingsTests cases); a failure that doesn't reproduce at the red head, fails at the green commit too, or reads as the build environment (full disk, MSB3883) blames no one; the tickets library has no reopen, so each untouched "Fails on main" ticket is superseded by one naming the culprit commit and its ticket, linked follow-up-of it (M.ORCH-T1687)) | 67a67bbd |

b8f0b08e Tree menu: the Launcher child row's rocket icon now overlays the same badge cell the other pane rows' status icon sits in, instead of rendering as a separate element after it, which reserved that empty badge cell's width in front of the rocket and shifted it a column right of every other row's icon (M.ORCH-T1798); 2d4b6520 Every context menu in the dashboard gets an icon-based alternative: a visible "more" button beside each row that owns one (the tree sidebar's login header and CLI/Launcher pane rows, the flat login tab strip, the flat CLI tab strip, the Save button), opening the exact same menu a right-click does with a tap or a left click, since right-click doesn't work on touch or in the phone layout. Every item in those menus (Rename, Copy PID, Change Color, Undock/Dock, Pop out, broadcast, Move to, Open Project and its project tree, Run/New Launcher, User Settings, Quick Save/Load All) now carries a leading icon glyph too, via a generalized icon+label header (MaDropdownMenuItem has no Icon presenter of its own to set) (M.ORCH-T1793); b7a26308 A hidden CLI tab holds at most 16 KB of output for its catch-up and asks the host for its screen beyond that: showing a Launcher tab still froze the dashboard for five seconds while a quarter of a megabyte of held redraws was drawn (M.ORCH-T1738); 73bb0f7d Milestone steward: orchestrator milestone steward and a daily daemon pass file one stamped ticket for each failed build or exists check of an active milestone that no open ticket covers, put it forward for the owner's approval, and list the milestone's closed tickets that came back or cite no evidence (M.ORCH-T1686); 12f35e60 Tree sidebar: the last branch connector draws an elbow, not a tee (M.ORCH-T1768); b9c57b4c Re-add the Save button's right-click Quick Save All / Quick Load All wiring to MainWindow.xaml.cs, reverted out by a concurrent M.ORCH-T1768 cleanup so this ticket could commit it itself (M.ORCH-T1769); 0ee5e0c2 The dashboard's Inbox has Approve and Decline buttons on an addition waiting to join an active milestone (M.ORCH-T1685); b40dbcfd Save button: retire Save all & close's force-close-and-exit, add Quick Save All / Quick Load All with a confirm and a completion-time modal (M.ORCH-T1769); 39053af0 The dashboard's Inbox has Approve and Decline buttons on an addition waiting to join an active milestone (M.ORCH-T1685); 260213f7 TaskList: unify the sidebar's Task List, live activity and ticket cards into one Active section (tasks and tickets side by side, not split by kind), keep Pending, and add the first 100 highest-priority open tickets as a third section; each row gets a Play button (jumps to the CLI and person working it, reusing Tickets Desktop's own "show who is working X" lookup) and a separate Ticket button (opens it in Tickets Desktop) instead of one whole-card click (M.ORCH-T1770); 8160bc28 Tree sidebar: a CLI node's context menu now matches its flat-tab twin, plus a QA pass restoring what the pre-merge lists could do (M.ORCH-T1768); 75529592 The owner inbox lists each addition waiting to join an active milestone and each milestone that has grown since activation, and orchestrator milestone gains pending, approve, decline and a Grown column (M.ORCH-T1685); 030286b9 Hide the Life Raft fallback viewer's non-functional terminal scrollbar (M.ORCH-T1792); 28f107d1 Guard ApplyFiguresAsync against overlapping status-stream pushes (M.ORCH-T1791); 8bcbc130 Key MoveToAccountAsync's re-entrancy guard by session, not by tab (M.ORCH-T1790); The global login's own tab is a known exception (noted on the ticket) since LoginScope.Tabs hardcodes it "signed in" (M.ORCH-T1821); eea6909e The CLI row's hover tooltip (LoginHoverTipTemplate's usage chart) now stretches to the tooltip's full width (HorizontalAlignment="Stretch", dropping the old hardcoded Width="200") instead of sitting narrower than the text line below it; its popup delay (ToolTipService.InitialShowDelay, hardcoded 0ms on both the flat tab strip and the tree header) becomes a live Vault setting, CliTooltipDelayMs, defaulting to 0ms (20% below the old 0ms is still 0, but it's now dialable instead of pinned) (M.ORCH-T1823); 92086dbd Login: every real login's right-click menu gets a Login item that re-authenticates it on its own, without the Logins modal (M.ORCH-T1820); e7645ecd StatusAggregator/LoginScope: a repo's RepoState.Working now includes its CLIs' running subagents, not only its own last transcript write - a CLI whose turn sat idle while a subagent it started kept working read Waiting or Dormant on its repo card, the per-login tab view (LoginScope.Keep re-derives Classify after filtering) and the daemon's "needs you" alert, even though the context gate already knew it was busy (AgentBoardRow.IsBusy) (M.ORCH-T1824); 9f11497a Tree sidebar: branch connectors use MaMuted (the zzz badge's own color) instead of MaChromeBorder, which also painted the selected row's own highlight and washed the spine out; sibling rows' connector columns now touch edge-to-edge (LoginTreeChildRow's old vertical margin moved onto TreePaneRow's content instead) so the spine reads as one continuous line ending in an L, never broken by row gaps (M.ORCH-T1822)) | superseded by M.ORCH-T1842: bisected to eea6909 |

acfb21e4 Plans button in the dashboard's menu bar: a lightbulb after the Inbox opens a list of saved plans - half-formed ideas and features with no implementation ticket yet, each a markdown file under docs\plans in the workspace root or any repo the snapshot knows. PlanCatalog reads each file's head for its title, status and summary, newest first; the folder, summary length and head size are Vault settings (M.ORCH-T1826); f4f4a7eb orchestrator busy: --all judges hosted CLIs by their real state, --running-only counts only work actually running, --skip-goal leaves out CLIs on a /goal; the redeploy gate's answer is unchanged (M.ORCH-T1827); 9bc8fa73 General/MindAttic workspace-root CLI tabs get a workspace identity icon: a plain home glyph now overlays the tree sidebar's and tab strip's badge cell (already wired on main, M.ORCH-T1823) for a tab opened at the workspace root rather than on a repo. It needed TerminalPaneViewModel.IsWorkspacePane/WorkspaceRoot, which this adds: AgentBoard.Build only ever walks registered repos' own sessions, so a workspace-root tab's AgentBoardRow is never found and none of its three status badges light, leaving the cell blank. WorkspaceRoot is pushed onto each pane when opened or reattached, and onto every open pane again if the owning TerminalsViewModel's own WorkspaceRoot is set later (a pane opened before the Vault settings load still gets its icon once they arrive) (M.ORCH-T1819); 25877bbd Log out: a signed-in login's right-click menu can sign it out, scoped to one account; while logged out its menu reduces to just Login and the rest of the dashboard treats it as a roster account never signed in here, via the same real state it already reads back, not a new flag. The global login's own tab is a known exception (noted on the ticket) since LoginScope.Tabs hardcodes it "signed in" (M.ORCH-T1821); eea6909e The CLI row's hover tooltip (LoginHoverTipTemplate's usage chart) now stretches to the tooltip's full width (HorizontalAlignment="Stretch", dropping the old hardcoded Width="200") instead of sitting narrower than the text line below it; its popup delay (ToolTipService.InitialShowDelay, hardcoded 0ms on both the flat tab strip and the tree header) becomes a live Vault setting, CliTooltipDelayMs, defaulting to 0ms (20% below the old 0ms is still 0, but it's now dialable instead of pinned) (M.ORCH-T1823); 92086dbd Login: every real login's right-click menu gets a Login item that re-authenticates it on its own, without the Logins modal (M.ORCH-T1820); e7645ecd StatusAggregator/LoginScope: a repo's RepoState.Working now includes its CLIs' running subagents, not only its own last transcript write - a CLI whose turn sat idle while a subagent it started kept working read Waiting or Dormant on its repo card, the per-login tab view (LoginScope.Keep re-derives Classify after filtering) and the daemon's "needs you" alert, even though the context gate already knew it was busy (AgentBoardRow.IsBusy) (M.ORCH-T1824); 9f11497a Tree sidebar: branch connectors use MaMuted (the zzz badge's own color) instead of MaChromeBorder, which also painted the selected row's own highlight and washed the spine out; sibling rows' connector columns now touch edge-to-edge (LoginTreeChildRow's old vertical margin moved onto TreePaneRow's content instead) so the spine reads as one continuous line ending in an L, never broken by row gaps (M.ORCH-T1822)) | passes on main@fab0293 |
